# The compute ladder

*Generated by `python -m r52.ladder` on 2026-09-13. Prices and peak-FLOPS figures retrieved 2026-09-13; see `r52/ladder/prices.yaml` and `r52/ladder/rungs.yaml` for a source URL on every row.*

**Method.** `FLOPs = 6 x N_active x D`; `GPU-hours = FLOPs / (peak_TFLOPS x MFU x 3600)`; `wall-clock = GPU-hours / n_GPUs`; `cost = GPU-hours x $/GPU-hour`. N is the *active* parameter count, which is why a 30B-A3B MoE and a 3B dense model cost the same to train. MFU is calibrated against three disclosed runs (below). Prices are the verified September-2026 floors from `research/04` §B.2: H100 spot $0.94, H100 on-demand $2.43. `—` means no number exists — never 0.

> The frontier row's dollar figures are **our own arithmetic** at 35% MFU on September-2026 rental prices, not a disclosure. Anthropic has published no GPU-hours, no FLOPs and no cost for Fable 5, Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and Epoch's cost article publishes trends, not per-model dollar figures. See `rungs.yaml` for the full caveat.

## Notes on each row

**Rung 0 -- GPT-2 small, from scratch, on a Mac Mini** — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §10 Run B: 124M params, seq 1024, <=0.75B tokens, target val loss <= 3.28. MFU 0.3052 is exactly the measured training-effective 1.3 TFLOPS divided by the 4.26 TFLOPS theoretical FP32 peak (both measured 2026-09-13, road-to-52 probe; the 1.3 figure was measured at 111M params, not 124M, so treat the wall-clock as +/- one bucket). The resulting ~119 h / ~5.0 days agrees with ARCHITECTURE §10's independent "4-6 days" estimate. Cost is the *marginal* cost of hardware we already own -- $0, not "free".

**Rung 1 -- nanochat-class 1B on a rented 8xH100 node** — Chinchilla-optimal 1B/20B, the "1B dense" row of research/04 §B.5 (1.20e20 FLOP, 96 H100-h @35% MFU, $91 spot / $234 on-demand). CAVEAT, and it matters: nanochat's own record run (Run 6, 2026-03-14) reached CORE 0.262634 in 1.65 h on 8xH100 -- 13.2 H100-hours, ~$20 spot / ~$40 on-demand -- i.e. roughly 7x cheaper than this row. nanochat does not disclose that run's exact N and D in either research/02 or research/04, so this row uses the Chinchilla-optimal 1B/20B shape rather than reverse-engineering them. The disclosed nanochat figures are carried verbatim in the `ref-nanochat-speedrun-record` row below; treat that row, not this one, as the real price of nanochat-class capability.

**Rung 2 -- 3B dense, Chinchilla-optimal** — research/04 §B.5 Chinchilla-optimal table: 1.08e21 FLOP, 867 H100-h @35%, $815 spot / $2.1k on-demand / 444 B200-h @30% ($1.6k). Four and a half node-days on one 8xH100 box. NO NAMED MODEL IS CLAIMED HERE. research/04 gives this rung's cost but no capability result, and the obvious same-size comparator does not hold: SmolLM3 is also 3B but saw 11.2T tokens, 187x this budget. The `beats` cell stays empty until we measure something.

**Rung 2 (MoE) -- 30B-A3B, Chinchilla-optimal on active params** — Identical cost to `rung-2-dense-3b` because training compute scales with *active* parameters. research/04 §B.5 reading 1: "The MoE active-parameter trick is the whole game... You get 30B of capacity for a 3B training bill. This is exactly why Qwen3-30B-A3B-shaped models exist, and why DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs a 552B backbone at 8B prefill / 16B decode." Inference memory is a different bill entirely and is not modelled here.

**Rung 2b -- 3B dense (or 30B-A3B) on 150B tokens: the $2,000 budget** — research/04 §B.5 "What $2,000 actually buys": at Prime Intellect spot ($0.94/H100-h), $2,000 = 2,128 H100-hours = 266 hours on an 8xH100 node = 11.1 node-days = 2.65e21 FLOP at 35% MFU, which is a 3B dense or 30B-A3B MoE on *147B* tokens. This row rounds to 150B, so it lands a little over budget ($2,037) -- the honest ceiling is 147B tokens for exactly $2,000. research/04's verdict on this rung: "The affordable rungs produce nothing that beats Fable 5.1 at anything general. The money must go into post-training, scaffolding, and inference."

**Rung 3 -- 8B dense, Chinchilla-optimal** — research/04 §B.5: 7.68e21 FLOP, 6.2k H100-h @35%, $5.8k spot / $15.0k on-demand / 3.2k B200-h @30% ($11.0k). Sized at 64 GPUs so the wall-clock is ~4 days rather than a month on one node; the dollar cost is unchanged, only the calendar is. Well past the $2,000 budget -- this rung needs a Prime Intellect Fast Compute Grant (research/04 §B.4: $500-$100,000, 5-10 day decisions, open to anyone) or Alliance/Fir time via a sponsoring McMaster PI.

**nanochat record (Run 6, 2026-03-14) -- 8xH100, 1.65 h** — research/04 §B.1 Tier 1 and research/02's speedruns table. CORE 0.262634, beating GPT-2 (1.6B)'s 0.256525. On-demand ~$40 @ $3/GPU-h, ~$20 spot. Time-to-GPT-2 fell 3.04 h -> 1.65 h in seven weeks; against the 2019 baseline, training time dropped 98.8% over seven years (168 h -> ~2 h). N and D are NOT disclosed in our sources, so no FLOPs, no implied MFU, and no computed cost for this row -- only what the leaderboard states. The $300/$1000 nanochat tiers are tagged UNVERIFIED in research/04 and are omitted.

**modded-nanogpt speedrun record #89 (2026-07-17) -- 124M to 3.28 val loss, 8xH100** — research/02: record 1.23 minutes, set 2026-07-17, via "MLP down projection in FP8 with efficient delayed scaling metric". Stack: Muon, FlashAttention-3, value embeddings, logit softcapping, FP8 quantization, paired-head attention, learnable XSA. This is the direct quality bar for Rung 0 -- same parameter count, same val-loss target (3.28), on 8xH100 in 73 seconds instead of ~5 days on one M4. Token count is not disclosed per-record, so no FLOPs are computed.

**SmolLM3 3B (HuggingFace) -- 384 H100s x 24 days** — research/04 §B.1 Tier 2 and §B.5's calibration table: 2.02e23 FLOP, 220k H100-h, implied MFU 25.7%. This is the low anchor of the MFU model -- small models and long-context-heavy recipes do not reach 35%.

**DeepSeek-V3 671B-A37B -- 2.788M H800-hours, $5.576M disclosed** — research/04 §B.5: the ladder's 35%/30% MFU choice "reproduces DeepSeek-V3's disclosed cost to within ~4%". The $5.576M figure is the official run only; DeepSeek explicitly notes the prior research and ablation budget was separate and much larger. Related datapoint (research/04 §B.1 Tier 3): DeepSeek-R1's RL stage alone was ~$294,000 (R1-Zero 648 H800 x ~198 h = 128k H800-h; R1 648 x ~80 h = 52k) on top of that base -- "the single most important datapoint here for a small team".

**Llama 3.1 405B dense -- 30.84M H100-hours** — research/04 §B.5's high anchor: 3.80e25 FLOP, 30.84M H100-h, implied MFU 34.6% (the Llama-3 family total was 39.3M H100-h: 1.46M for 8B, 7.0M for 70B). Epoch's independent read (16k H100s x 380 TFLOP/s x 6.25M s = 3.8e25 FLOP, ~72 days) implies 38.4%. The token count here is 15.6T; research/04 states "15T+" and quotes the FLOPs as 3.80e25, which pins D at ~15.6T.

**Kimi K2 scale -- 1T-A32B MoE, 15.5T tokens (modelled, nothing disclosed)** — research/04 §B.5 overtrained table: 2.98e24 FLOP, 2.39M H100-h @35%, $2.24M spot / $5.80M on-demand. MODELLED, NOT DISCLOSED -- research/04 §B.1: "No Chinese frontier lab disclosed GPU-hours or FLOPs for any 2026 model (Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek V4). All UNVERIFIED."

**Kimi K3 scale -- 2.8T-A104B MoE, 15T tokens (modelled, nothing disclosed)** — research/04 §B.5 overtrained table: 9.36e24 FLOP, 7.51M H100-h @35%, $7.06M spot / $18.25M on-demand. MODELLED, NOT DISCLOSED (see `ref-kimi-k2-scale`). Kimi K3 is the best open model on Epoch's ECI (157.6) and is the open-weight model that beat Claude Fable 5.1 on GPQA Diamond -- so this row is the honest price tag on "best open weights", and it is three orders of magnitude past the $2,000 budget.

**Frontier (Fable-class), 2026 -- 1e26 to 1e27 FLOP** — research/04 §B.1 Tier 4: "Frontier 2026 runs: 1e26 - 1e27 FLOP; ~$200-500M/run (GPT-5 / Gemini Ultra class)" -- tagged UNVERIFIED secondary, and research/04 adds the important correction that "Epoch's cost article does not publish per-model dollar figures... Per-model 2026 cost claims on secondary sites are NOT Epoch-sourced." ANTHROPIC HAS DISCLOSED NOTHING for Fable 5 / Fable 5.1 / Opus 5: no GPU-hours, no FLOPs, no cost. The dollar figures this ladder prints for this row are our own 6ND-style arithmetic at 35% MFU on September-2026 rental prices, not a disclosure and not an Epoch estimate. What Epoch does publish (research/04 §B.1 Tier 4): frontier training cost has grown 2.4x/year since 2016 (95% CI 2.0-3.1x); hardware is 47-67% of cost, R&D staff 29-49%, energy 2-6%; and "the largest training runs will cost more than a billion dollars by 2027". research/04 §B.5 reading 2: "The frontier is 1e26-1e27 FLOP; this ladder's largest row is 9.4e24. A student is two orders of magnitude short at minimum."
